name: English

_purpose.*_file: file names teamcall writes into the company's folder; the person sees them in their file list, so plain words in their language; {who} and {name} stay as they are
_purpose.charter_*: the pilot charter, read by the manager who sponsors the pilot
_purpose.fast_*: the 20-minute fast path card, read by one employee who has never used a terminal
_purpose.ch_*: the 5-hour champion path, read by the employee who will help colleagues
_purpose.boost_*: termboost: the same task once in the app and once in the terminal, then again with one command
_purpose.report_*: the pilot report for the company; it never names a person, only P1, P2, ...
_purpose.decide_*: a one-page decision for the manager: scale, fix and repeat, or stop
_purpose.rule_*: a per-program rule, said in one short line when that program is listed
_purpose.note_*: one line about how this computer's Claude Code is signed in

kept: already there, left as it is: {path}
charter_promise: In 30 days {people} people of the company go from the usual chat to working with an agent in the terminal, and the company grows to {target} people through its own champions. For every person the journal keeps the attempt, the time to the first working result, the workflow actually built, the help it took and, when someone stopped, the reason.
charter_waves_how: Weeks 1-2: the first people take the fast path and the first champion takes the 5-hour path. Weeks 3-4: each champion brings in about {per} colleagues with the same fast path.
charter_goal_text: At least {goal} working results confirmed among the first {people} people.
charter_key_metric: The key number: minutes of human help per successful first result.
m_coverage_example: 40 files processed instead of a sample of 10
m_repeatable_example: the work runs every week with one command
m_capability_example: the employee built a working tool of their own for the first time
m_risk_example: which parts a person still reviews
charter_setup: How the pilot is set up (one page for IT)
setup_devices: Devices: the company's computers, or own laptops on the company's route (gatecall, step B2).
setup_accounts: Accounts: one seat per person (Claude Team, or the seat the company already pays for - see `teamcall agents`).
setup_data: Data: work files and training files of the pilot; red folders stay with a model on the computer (gatecall).
setup_folders: Folders: the pilot's folder; the agent works on a copy until the person has seen the list of changes (safecall).
setup_review: Review: a person reads every result before it leaves the team; a second opinion from another company's AI on the important ones (duocall).
setup_install: Install and remove: one command each (the fast path card); removing deletes the program and its settings.
setup_contact: Contact when something goes wrong: the sponsor and the champion.
setup_actions: Sending, buying and publishing outside the company stay with the person: the agent prepares, the person presses.
setup_retention: Keeping and deleting: the journal and the reports stay in the company's folder; pilot copies are deleted on day 30.
setup_red_from_policy: Red folders from the company policy:
setup_providers_from_policy: AI vendors the company policy allows:
gives_people: people who really work at a computer
gives_devices: approved devices, AI accounts, kinds of data and test tasks
gives_payer: who pays for the seats (billcall counts it)
gives_measure: the first and the last measurement
gives_case: the right to describe the case without names
charter_next: Next: `teamcall fast --person <name>` for each person, `teamcall champion --person <name>` for the champion, and `teamcall log add` after each step.
fast_task_default: a real task from this week's work
fast_install_how: Open the terminal and paste: `{install}`. Then open a new terminal window and type `claude --version`.
fast_sign_in: Sign in with the work seat
fast_sign_in_how: Type `claude` and sign in in the browser with the company's account (claude.ai). Signed in this way, the phone works as a remote later.
fast_first_task_how: In a copy of the work folder say: "first a plan, then do it" and give the task: {task}. Read the plan, say yes, look at the result.
fast_claudemd: CLAUDE.md: the rules the agent reads every time
fast_claudemd_how: Ask: "write a CLAUDE.md for this folder: who I am, what I do here, three rules". Short direct instructions, at most {max} lines (`teamcall claudemd CLAUDE.md` checks).
fast_repeat_how: Turn the task into a command of its own (`teamcall boost`), then run it again with `/` and its name.
fast_log: Done? The champion writes it down: `teamcall log add --person "{person}" --stage first_artifact`.
champion_intro: The champion helps about {per} colleagues through the fast path and knows where people get stuck.
ch_plan_mode_how: Plan mode (Shift+Tab), what the agent asks before acting, and the folder copy before changes.
ch_claudemd: The team's CLAUDE.md and shared settings
ch_claudemd_how: One CLAUDE.md per team folder under 100 lines; `.claude/settings.json` shared in the folder.
ch_skills: The company's own skills and plugin
ch_skills_how: Turn the three most repeated tasks into skills and a company plugin (firmcall).
ch_second_opinion_how: A different company's AI checks the important results (duocall, sidecall); `teamcall agents` shows what the company's seats already include.
ch_remote_how: Remote Control and cloud sessions for work on the road (pocketcall).
ch_unblock_how: Read the journal (`teamcall log show`): who stopped at which step and why; the most frequent blocker gets fixed for everyone.
ch_measure_how: Before and after on one real task per person (`teamcall measure`), then `teamcall report`.
boost_title: The same task in the app and in the terminal: {name}
boost_term_1: the same folder opens with the agent
boost_app_3: next week: write it all again
boost_schedule: Next time it is one command: `/{name}` inside Claude Code, or `claude -p "/{name}"` from a schedule.
boost_skill_body:
Do this task in the current folder, the same way as last time: {task}

First say the plan in two lines, then do it, then list what changed.
claudemd_too_long: CLAUDE.md has {n} lines; keep it to {max} short direct instructions - a long one is read worse.
report_no_names: People are P1, P2, ... - no names in this report.
report_key_metric: Minutes of human help per successful first result
decision_repeat: Fix the blockers and repeat with the same people
decide_why_scale: {succeeded} of {count} people reached a first working result, {champions} champion(s), {help} minutes of help per result (limit {max}).
decide_why_repeat: {succeeded} of {count} people reached a first working result, {champions} champion(s), {help} minutes of help per result (limit {max}): not yet 3 of every 5 with a champion within the limit.
decide_why_stop: No first working result among {count} people.
decide_next_scale: Each champion brings in about 8 colleagues with the fast path; the seats are counted with billcall before buying.
decide_next_repeat: Take the most frequent blocker from the report, fix it for everyone, and run the fast path again for those who stopped.
decide_next_stop: Read where each person stopped; try branch B (Cowork or the app's Code tab) with the same task, then measure again.
move_title: Moving people to the terminal in 30 days
move_intro: Fast path for everyone in 20 minutes, one champion per team, and for each program the seat that already pays for it.
move_w1: the first 5 people: fast path; the first champion starts the 5-hour path
move_w2: each person turns one weekly task into a command (`teamcall boost`); measurement before and after
move_w3: champions bring in the next wave; the most frequent blocker is fixed for everyone
move_w4: report and decision: scale or stop (`teamcall report`, `teamcall decide`)
move_programs: Programs, and what pays for them
agents_title: Terminal agents and the seats that already pay for them
rule_copy_only_prepaid: works on a cleaned copy, with a prepaid balance
rule_training_only: works in a training folder (it has no read-only switch)
rule_no_blanket_permission: gets permissions one by one, never one for everything
note_api_key: Claude Code here signs in with an API key: the phone remote and cloud sessions need the claude.ai sign-in of a seat.
note_base_url: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points away from Anthropic: the phone remote is off in this window.
note_traffic: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC or DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK is set: the phone remote is off.
note_signed_in: Claude Code here is signed in with a claude.ai account.
